key_insight: In symmetry-preserving VQE circuits, generator connectivity—not circuit depth alone—determines whether the ansatz can access the full many-body symmetry sector and reach high-fidelity ground states.
engineering_relevance: A minimal, well-chosen symmetry-preserving connectivity upgrade can dramatically improve quantum simulation performance, reducing the need to stack deeper circuits that still remain variationally restricted.
method: Studied symmetry-preserving nearest-neighbor circuits for the XXZ and Hubbard models via dynamical Lie algebra analysis.
Added one minimal extra generator: a next-to-nearest-neighbor single-excitation for XXZ or a correlated double-excitation for Hubbard.
Compared how these connectivity changes expand the accessible manifold and improve VQE ground-state optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the restricted circuits work near free-fermion limits, but interactions expose inaccessible directions; the minimal connectivity change reconstructs the full orthogonal DLA and yields near-unit ground-state fidelity in VQE simulations.
watch_item: The required generator modification is model-specific, so identifying the right symmetry-preserving connectivity may still be nontrivial for new Hamiltonians or hardware-constrained layouts.
paper_title: Connectivity Controls Variational Accessibility in Symmetry-Preserving Quantum Circuits
